corrections.prior: Deoxyribonucleic acid; the nucleotide polymer that stores hereditary information in most organisms.
corrections.corrected: Deoxyribonucleic acid: a long molecule whose sequence of chemical units carries hereditary information.

corrections.prior: One continuous DNA molecule with associated proteins and organized genes and regulatory regions.
corrections.corrected: An organized DNA–protein structure. Before copying, it contains one DNA molecule. After copying, it contains two attached copies; when they separate, each is counted as a chromosome.

corrections.prior: A DNA region whose transcription contributes to a functional RNA or protein product, together with relevant regulation.
corrections.corrected: A region of DNA whose information contributes to a functional RNA molecule or protein.

corrections.prior: One of a pair of chromosomes with corresponding loci, one typically inherited from each parent, though alleles may differ.
corrections.corrected: Two chromosomes with corresponding gene positions, usually one inherited from each parent; they may carry different versions of the same genes.

corrections.prior: A chromosome region where sister chromatids remain joined and the kinetochore assembles.
corrections.corrected: A chromosome region involved in joining sister chromatids and attaching the chromosome to the cell-division machinery.

corrections.prior: The semiconservative copying of DNA before cell division.
corrections.corrected: Copying DNA so that each resulting double-stranded molecule has one original strand and one newly made strand.

corrections.prior: A microtubule-based structure that attaches to and moves chromosomes during cell division.
corrections.corrected: A system of protein fibres that positions and moves chromosomes during cell division.

corrections.prior: A protein complex assembled at the centromere that attaches a chromosome to spindle microtubules.
corrections.corrected: A protein attachment structure at a chromosome’s centromere that connects it to spindle fibres.

corrections.prior: The division stage when chromosomes align at the cell's metaphase plate and attach to spindle structures.
corrections.corrected: A division stage in which chromosomes align near the middle of the cell with attachments to the spindle.

corrections.prior: A haploid reproductive cell that can grow by mitosis into a multicellular haploid organism without gamete fusion.
corrections.corrected: In the plant life cycles studied here, a haploid reproductive cell that grows by cell division into the haploid stage without first joining another reproductive cell.

corrections.prior: A molecule built from amino acids whose sequence and folded structure contribute to biological function.
corrections.corrected: A molecule made of a chain or chains of small building blocks called amino acids; its sequence and folded shape help determine its function.

corrections.prior: The information-bearing part of a nucleotide: A, T, G or C in ordinary DNA, with U replacing T in RNA.
corrections.corrected: One of the information-bearing chemical units in DNA or RNA; ordinary DNA uses A, T, G and C, while RNA usually uses U in place of T.

corrections.prior: The proportion of individuals in a population that have a particular genotype.
corrections.corrected: The relative numbers or probabilities of specified genotype classes, written in a stated order; for example, AA:Aa:aa = 1:2:1.

corrections.prior: The probability of a scored characteristic after translating genotype possibilities through the inheritance model.
corrections.corrected: The relative numbers or probabilities of specified observable trait classes, written in a stated order; for example, dominant:recessive = 3:1 in a simple complete-dominance cross.

corrections.prior: Tendency of loci on the same chromosome to be inherited together, especially when they are physically close.
corrections.corrected: Gene positions on the same chromosome; nearby positions tend to be inherited together because crossing over separates them less often.

corrections.prior: A change in DNA sequence that can create a new allele when inherited.
corrections.corrected: A change in DNA sequence that can create a new allele; whether it reaches offspring depends on the cell lineage and reproduction.

corrections.prior: Ribonucleic acid, a nucleic acid with ribose and typically uracil that has informational, adaptor and catalytic roles.
corrections.corrected: Ribonucleic acid: a molecule related to DNA whose chemical units usually use U instead of T; different RNAs carry information, help assemble proteins or carry out other cellular functions.

corrections.prior: A building block joined by peptide bonds into a polypeptide.
corrections.corrected: One of the small chemical building blocks joined into a protein chain.
